# Harvest Grocery Holdings - Outside Development and IP Playbook

## 1 General Approach

Comment only on terms that change risk or value. Where the fee is fixed and the work is
bespoke, the primary commercial question is what Harvest owns and can do when the engagement
ends. Escalate any departure from a position marked non-negotiable.

## 2 Ownership of Deliverables

Harvest must own all deliverables developed under a statement of work, including source
code, trained model weights and parameters, feature definitions, evaluation artifacts, and
documentation. Ownership must be effected by a present assignment of all right, title, and
interest, and may not be conditioned on anything other than payment of undisputed fees. A
license back to the supplier is acceptable only for the supplier's genuinely pre-existing
materials and for residual general knowledge retained in unaided memory. A structure in
which the supplier owns the deliverables and grants Harvest a license is a non-negotiable
departure. Escalate.

## 3 Background Technology and Embedded Licenses

A supplier may keep ownership of technology it owned before the engagement or developed
independently of it. Definitions of "background technology," "tools," or "know-how" must be
limited to materials that exist before the applicable statement of work or that are
developed outside the engagement without use of Harvest data, and must exclude anything
conceived or created in performing the services. Where background materials are embedded in
a deliverable, Harvest requires a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free,
sublicensable license to use, modify, and have modified those materials as part of the
deliverable, without an internal-use restriction. Read the ownership section and the
background section together: a broad background definition can hollow out an ownership
clause that reads correctly on its own.

## 4 Harvest Data

Harvest data supplied for a project may be used solely to perform that project. A supplier
may not use Harvest data, or features, embeddings, statistics, benchmarks, or other data
derived from it, to develop, train, tune, or benchmark models, products, or services for any
other customer, whether or not the data is aggregated, de-identified, or anonymized. Data
and derived data must be deleted or returned within thirty days after the project ends,
subject only to routine backup retention. Any supplier right to reuse Harvest data is a
non-negotiable departure. Escalate.

## 5 Acceptance and Payment

Deliverables must be subject to written acceptance criteria stated in the statement of work.
Where a statement of work specifies a performance metric, acceptance must be tested against
that metric on a holdout data set. Harvest requires a defined acceptance period, a right to
reject with written reasons, a supplier cure period, and a refund of amounts paid for a
deliverable that is not cured. Milestone payments must fall due on acceptance rather than on
delivery, and at least twenty-five percent of fixed fees should remain payable only on final
acceptance.

## 6 Personnel and Subcontracting

Key personnel must be named in the statement of work and may not be replaced without notice
and reasonable consultation. Subcontracting, including use of supplier affiliates and
offshore delivery centers, requires Harvest's prior written consent. Each approved
subcontractor must be under a written agreement that flows down the confidentiality,
data-use, and intellectual-property assignment obligations of the engagement, and the
supplier remains responsible for subcontractor performance. Delivery locations must be
disclosed before work begins.

## 7 Liability and Warranty

A general liability cap equal to fees paid and payable under the applicable statement of
work is acceptable. Breaches of confidentiality, breaches of the data-use restrictions in
Section 4, and supplier indemnification obligations should sit outside that cap. A
workmanlike-services warranty is acceptable where acceptance testing under Section 5 carries
the performance risk.

# DataCraft Labs Professional Services Agreement

This Professional Services Agreement (this "Agreement") is entered into by DataCraft Labs,
Inc. ("Consultant") and Harvest Grocery Holdings, LLC ("Client").

## 1.1 Services and Statements of Work

Consultant will perform the professional services described in one or more statements of
work signed by both parties (each, a "SOW"). Each SOW is governed by this Agreement. A SOW
may add to or vary the terms of this Agreement for the project it describes, and in the
event of a conflict the terms of the SOW control for that project.

## 2.1 Fees and Expenses

Client will pay the fees stated in each SOW. Work outside the scope described in a SOW is
performed on a time-and-materials basis at Consultant's then-current rate card and requires
a signed change order. Client will reimburse pre-approved travel expenses. All amounts are
exclusive of taxes.

## 3.1 Term and Termination

This Agreement begins on the Effective Date and continues for two years unless terminated
earlier. Either party may terminate this Agreement or any SOW for convenience on thirty (30)
days written notice, and Client will pay for Services performed and expenses incurred
through the effective date of termination. Sections 5.1, 6.1, 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, and 9.1 survive
termination.

## 4.1 Personnel

Consultant will assign personnel with skills and experience suitable for the Services. A SOW
may identify individuals as key personnel. Consultant may reassign, replace, or change the
allocation of any personnel, including individuals identified as key personnel, in its sole
discretion, provided that the Services continue to be performed by qualified personnel.

## 4.2 Subcontracting

Consultant may perform any portion of the Services through its affiliates, independent
contractors, and offshore delivery centers, in any location, without notice to or consent
from Client, and may disclose Client Confidential Information and Client Data to those
persons to the extent Consultant considers necessary for the engagement. Consultant will
require each such person to comply with confidentiality obligations no less protective than
those Consultant applies to its own confidential information of a similar nature. Consultant
remains responsible for the performance of the Services.

## 5.1 Confidentiality

Each party will protect the other party's Confidential Information with at least reasonable
care and will use it only as necessary to exercise its rights and perform its obligations
under this Agreement. These obligations continue for three (3) years after disclosure and,
for information that constitutes a trade secret, for as long as it remains a trade secret
under applicable law.

## 6.1 Client Materials

"Client Materials" means the data, systems, content, and other materials that Client makes
available to Consultant, including any Client Data defined in a SOW. As between the parties,
Client owns all right, title, and interest in the Client Materials. Client grants Consultant
a non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use the Client Materials during the term of the
applicable SOW solely as necessary to perform the Services, except as otherwise provided in
a SOW.

## 7.1 Ownership of Work Product

"Work Product" means all deliverables, software, source code, model architectures, trained
model weights and parameters, feature definitions, notebooks, reports, and documentation
that Consultant creates in the course of performing the Services. All Work Product, and all
intellectual property rights in the Work Product, are and will remain the exclusive property
of Consultant. Subject to Client's payment of all amounts due, Consultant grants Client a
non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-sublicensable license to use and execute the
Deliverables solely for Client's internal business purposes. Client will not distribute,
resell, host for, or otherwise make the Deliverables available to any third party, and will
not modify the Deliverables or prepare derivative works of them except through Services
performed by Consultant.

## 7.2 Background Technology

"Background Technology" means all software, tools, libraries, model architectures,
feature-engineering methods, pipelines, templates, and know-how owned, developed, or
acquired by Consultant at any time, including any of the foregoing that is conceived,
created, or reduced to practice in the course of performing the Services and that is of
general application or that constitutes an improvement to or a derivative of materials
Consultant used or possessed before the applicable SOW. The Deliverables incorporate
Background Technology. Nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers ownership of any
Background Technology, and Client's rights in Background Technology embedded in a Deliverable
are coextensive with the license granted in Section 7.1.

## 7.3 Residual Knowledge

Consultant may use the general skills, knowledge, and experience that its personnel retain
in unaided memory as a result of performing the Services, provided that Consultant does not
use or disclose Client Confidential Information in doing so.

## 8.1 Warranties

Consultant warrants that the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike
manner by qualified personnel. Except as expressly stated in a SOW, Consultant does not
warrant that any model, forecast, or other output will achieve any particular level of
accuracy or produce any particular business result. Except for the express warranties in
this Section, the Deliverables are provided "as is" and Consultant disclaims all implied
warranties.

## 9.1 Limitation of Liability

Neither party's aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement will exceed
the fees paid and payable under the applicable SOW, except that this limit does not apply to
a party's breach of Section 5.1, to Consultant's use of Client Materials in violation of
Section 6.1, or to Consultant's indemnification obligations. Neither party is liable for
indirect, incidental, or consequential damages.

## 10.1 Governing Law

This Agreement is governed by the laws of the State of California, without regard to its
conflict-of-laws rules. The parties consent to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and
federal courts located in San Francisco County, California.

action.title: Ownership Clause Favors Supplier Over Customer
action.analysis: The PSA §7.1 states that all Work Product, including deliverables, software, source code, model architectures, trained model weights and parameters, feature definitions, notebooks, reports, and documentation, remains the exclusive property of the supplier (DataCraft). This clause does not align with the Harvest playbook which mandates that Harvest must own all deliverables developed under a statement of work, including source code, trained model weights and parameters, feature definitions, evaluation artifacts, and documentation. The playbook also emphasizes that ownership must be effected by a present assignment of all right, title, and interest, and may not be conditioned on anything other than payment of undisputed fees.
action.recommendation: Harvest should negotiate for ownership of all deliverables developed under the statement of work, including source code, trained model weights and parameters, feature definitions, evaluation artifacts, and documentation. This is a non-negotiable requirement according to the playbook.

action.recommendation: Harvest should negotiate for a narrower definition of Background Technology that excludes deliverables developed under the statement of work.

read_document.description: Read a document from the matter file, either in full or one numbered section.

section.description: Optional section number such as '4.2'. Omit for full text.

search_matter.description: Case-insensitive substring search across every document section.

query.description: Search phrase, three or more characters.

citations.description: Provision citations such as 'msa §4.2'. Operative provision first.

quotes.description: Optional verbatim quotations supporting the issue. Text must appear verbatim in the cited section; paraphrase belongs in analysis.

propose_redline.description: Propose replacement language for one section. Target the operative provision of the issue; link it to your submitted issue by reusing your issue_id label.

revise_redline.description: Replace the latest redline for an existing issue and provision. Only the latest version for that issue/document/section target is used for scoring.

submit_final.description: Submit the final summary for the supervising lawyer and end the episode. Submit only after all issues and redlines are in.

learned_facts.engagement: Custom demand-forecasting model built on the customer's historical sales data
learned_facts.deal_value: $400,000 fixed fee plus time-and-materials change orders
learned_facts.leverage: Balanced. DataCraft was selected from three shortlisted bidders and the fee is mid-market, so neither side is required to concede on everything.

action.replacement_text: "Background Technology" means all software, tools, libraries, model architectures, feature-engineering methods, pipelines, templates, and know-how owned, developed, or acquired by Consultant at any time, excluding any deliverables, software, source code, model architectures, trained model weights and parameters, feature definitions, notebooks, reports, and documentation that Consultant creates in the course of performing the Services. Background Technology must be limited to materials that exist before the applicable statement of work or that are developed outside the engagement without use of Harvest data, and must exclude anything conceived or created in performing the services.
action.rationale: This redline narrows the definition of Background Technology to exclude deliverables developed under the statement of work, ensuring that the ownership clause is not hollowed out.
